title: WorkersSpawnParams
description: Parameters for the workers.spawn agent tool: start one worker in a terminal pane of its own and hand it a task. The person may be asked to approve it first, and a refusal is an answer. Nothing you do after this keeps the worker supervised — nocx watches it whether or not you ask again.

command.description: The command line that starts the worker, exactly as a person would type it — for example `claude`. It runs in the worker's own pane.

task.description:
What this worker is for, in your own words. nocx TYPES this into the worker's own pane as soon as it is ready for input — this is how the worker is told what to do, not only a record of it — and it is also recorded, so a later workers.holdings can tell you what you started even if you have lost the context you started it from. A pane that stops on a question of its agent's own before it is ready — a folder-trust question, an approval — does not fail the call: the worker is live, nothing is typed, and the result says so in taskTyped and waitingOn. Answering that question with workers.answer is enough to deliver the task too — nocx types it itself the moment the pane is ready, and reports what became of it in that call's own task field, so do not call workers.spawn again or send the task any other way. A pane that never becomes ready for any other reason fails the whole call rather than leaving a worker nobody told anything; workers.say can hand a worker something more once it is running, but this is how its first task arrives.

TELL THE WORKER HOW TO REPORT, in this task, or it cannot: nocx will know when its process ends and will never know what it produced, and the record will say `abandoned` rather than `completed`. The instruction to include is exactly this — when you are finished, write to the file named by the NOCX_AGENT_REPORT environment variable: the first line `ok` or `fail`, and after it a few lines saying what you produced. Nothing else counts as reporting, and a worker that never writes it is not a failure — it is a worker nobody was told about.

result.title: WorkersSpawnResult
result.description: The worker that now exists. It is live: its enrolment arrived, which is what proves the agent started — never that this call returned. Live is not the same as told: taskTyped says whether the task reached the worker.

state.description: Always live: a spawn that did not reach live is an error, not a result.

taskTyped.description: True when the task was typed into the worker's pane. False when its pane stopped on a question of its agent's own first — waitingOn then says which kind — and nothing was typed: the worker is live and supervised, and it has not been told what to do.

waitingOn.description: Present only when taskTyped is false because the pane is asking something. permission_choice: the agent raised a question of its own, such as a tool approval or whether to trust the directory it was started in, and answering it answers the agent. modal_choice: a menu is open that the agent did not raise. Either way, answer it with workers.answer — that call is enough to deliver the task too, once the pane is ready; its own result says what became of it.
